Task Guide: Task: Simulate the thermal conductivity of a Lennard-Jones (LJ) system in LAMMPS. Define a simulation box with dimensions 10×10×20 in reduced LJ units. Set the number density of the fluid to 0.6 and the initial temperature to 1.35 in LJ units. Use a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice to initialize atomic positions and assign a Lennard-Jones potential with a cutoff of 2.5σ. Create two temperature-controlled regions: a hot region at the bottom (z = 0 to 1) and a cold region at the top (z = 10 to 11). First, equilibrate the system using the NVT ensemble at 1.35 temperature for 1000 timesteps with a temperature damping factor of 0.5, then switch to the NVE ensemble while applying Langevin thermostats to the hot and cold regions to maintain temperatures at 1.70 and 1.0, respectively, using damping factor of 1.0 for both thermostats. Track the energy added and removed by the thermostats and compute the temperature difference between the regions. Run the simulation for 10,000 timesteps to establish a steady-state temperature gradient. Afterward, reset the Langevin energy accumulation and continue the simulation for an additional 20,000 timesteps while calculating the running average of the temperature difference. Divide the simulation box into bins along the z-direction and compute the temperature profile over time. Use the heat flux and steady-state temperature gradient to compute the thermal conductivity using Fourier’s law. As the final output, return the thermal conductivity in Lennard-Jones (LJ) reduced units. This is a large simulation, hence it is advisable to use multiple CPUs. Make sure all the associated files for this task (input files, log files, any other files) are in the /results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/react/gpt_4o/brief/task_7/task_7_trial_2 directory. You can use the available I/O tools (e.g., write_file) make new files .etc. Whatever potentials you need to run the simulation, you can find them at /potentials/. A type of potential can be accessed by /potentials/TYPE where TYPE can be [EAM, TERSOFF, REAXFF] which further contains the exact potential files. Note that in case of reaxff potentials, pair style 'reax/c' has been renamed to 'reaxff' and always use NULL for the control file (cfile), for example, this syntax is correct : pair_style reaxff NULL. If the task is to give the final output as a scalar, only return the numerical value, without any units.

Action Input: {"path": "/results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/react/gpt_4o/brief/task_7/task_7_trial_2/in.lj_thermal_conductivity", "content": "units lj
atom_style atomic

# Create simulation box
dimension 3
boundary p p p
lattice fcc 0.6
region box block 0 10 0 10 0 20
create_box 1 box
create_atoms 1 box

# Define LJ potential
pair_style lj/cut 2.5
pair_coeff 1 1 1.0 1.0 2.5

# Define regions for thermostats
region hot block INF INF INF INF 0 1
region cold block INF INF INF INF 10 11

# Initial velocities
temperature 1.35
velocity all create 1.35 12345

# Equilibrate with NVT ensemble
fix 1 all nvt temp 1.35 1.35 0.5
run 1000

# Switch to NVE ensemble
unfix 1
fix 2 all nve
fix hot all langevin 1.70 1.70 1.0 12345 region hot
fix cold all langevin 1.0 1.0 1.0 12345 region cold

# Track energy added/removed by thermostats
compute ke all ke/atom
compute pe all pe/atom
compute temp all temp
thermo_style custom step temp etotal
thermo 100

# Run simulation to establish steady-state
timestep 0.005
run 10000

# Reset Langevin energy accumulation
fix_modify hot energy yes
fix_modify cold energy yes

# Continue simulation and calculate temperature profile
run 20000

# Output temperature profile
fix 3 all ave/spatial 1 100 1000 z lower 0.1 c_temp file temp.profile

# Calculate thermal conductivity
# (This part will be done post-simulation using the output data)
"}
